name: ScrollIndicator
description: Animated affordance at the base of a hero that scrolls to the next section.

ariaRequirements: Renders a real <button>, so it is focusable and activates on Enter and Space
aria-label or a visible label names the destination when no text is shown
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-07-24 — promotion pass: real <button> with Enter/Space activation and a focus-visible ring; every motion preset (bounce/pulse/fade) is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion (falls back to a static, fully-opaque icon); forced-colors keeps the icon and focus ring visible; light and dark legibility confirmed in a real browser. AT snapshots captured across base/light/dark/forced-colors.

governance.note: Promoted to stable: consumed by HomeHero, ProjectHero, BlogHero and AboutHero. The variant/position/motion axes are prop-sourced (Tailwind conditional classes + a GSAP motion preset), not root CVA.

content.voice: A short imperative naming the destination, not the gesture.

terminology.rationale: Names where the user lands. The gesture is already implied by the affordance and is wrong for keyboard and AT users.

content.notes: The label is optional. When omitted the control still needs an accessible name naming the destination.

targetId.description: ID of the target element to scroll to

motion.description: Looping motion applied to the icon as a hint to scroll.

speed.description: Duration of one motion half-cycle, in seconds.

distance.description: Vertical travel of the bounce motion, in pixels (bounce only).

forbiddenUse: (must): render it as a `<div>` with a click handler -- it must stay a real button so it is reachable by Tab and activates on both Enter and Space.
use it as general in-page navigation. It communicates "there is more below", not "jump to section". Use a link or `Breadcrumb` for navigation.
stack more than one on a page. Two scroll cues in one viewport contradict each other about where the reader should go next.
rely on the animation to carry meaning. It is suppressed under reduced motion, so the label and accessible name must stand alone.
dense: hero-footer scroll cue; animated icon (chevron/arrow/mouse) with optional label; motion bounce/pulse/fade/none gated by prefers-reduced-motion; real <button> that scrolls targetId into view

usage.description: ScrollIndicator is a hero-footer affordance that signals there is more page below and scrolls to it when activated. It renders a real button that scrolls a named target into view, with a looping motion hint on the icon that is suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

bestPractices.description: Give it a targetId matching a real element on the page so activation scrolls somewhere; without it the control renders but does nothing.
Prefer a label that names the destination (See our work), not the gesture (Scroll down); the label is also the accessible name.
Place it once, at the bottom of the first viewport, using position=center unless the hero copy already occupies the centre.
Do not rely on the motion to carry meaning; it is dropped under reduced motion, so the label and accessible name must stand alone.
Do not use it as general in-page navigation; it communicates there is more below, not jump to section. Use a link or Breadcrumb for that.
Do not stack more than one per viewport; two scroll cues contradict each other about where the reader should go next.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: The scroll cue glyph (chevron, arrow, or mouse) that carries the looping motion hint.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Optional visible text above the icon; when present it is also the accessible name and should name the destination.
